items.title: Australia's migrant policy offers lessons for EU and US
items.description: Australia has used offshore processing centers to deter asylum seekers for more than two decades. As the EU and US pursue similar third-country arrangements, Australia's experience highlights the potential problems.

items.title: Yemeni military says it has 'secured' Red Sea waterway
items.description: Saudi-backed forces gave conflicting reports of whether they had also seized the port city of Mokha, near the Bab al-Mandab Strait.

items.title: Germany news: Far-right AfD gets first house speaker in a German state parliament
items.description: For the first time since World War II, a far-right party has a house speaker in a German state parliament. And Germany's foreign minister has warned that the climate crisis could fuel extremism. DW has more.

items.title: US supreme court hears big oil’s bid to block climate damage lawsuits
items.description: <p>How the court will lean is unclear amid Suncor Energy and ExxonMobil’s attempt to stop lawsuits at state level</p><p>The <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/us-supreme-court">US supreme court</a> began its new nine-month term hearing arguments on Monday in a major <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/feb/23/supreme-court-suncor-exxonmobil-case">case</a> in which big oil companies attempted to strike a fatal blow against lawsuits

items.title: Merz, Macron seek tougher EU measures against unfair trade
items.description: Emmanuel Macron and Friedrich Merz have written to Ursula von der Leyen, calling for tougher EU mechanisms against unfair trade practices by other states. They name no names but seem to have China or the US in mind.

items.title: India news: Opposition leaders march towards Election Commission
items.description: India's opposition is amping up pressure on Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to resign over alleged voter roll manipulation. DW has more.

items.title: Euro plummets against US dollar: Has the next financial crisis begun?
items.description: The euro has fallen to a 17-month low against the dollar. That will make inflation worse in the EU, where political worries and concern over French debt are already troubling investors. Is a fiscal crisis at hand?
